subject: [PATCH v8 13/30] mm: handle PMD swap entries in fork path

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Zi Yan suggested rephrasing the handling of memory allocation failures in copy_huge_pmd() to clarify that -EIO should be returned for GFP_ATOMIC failures, allowing the caller to retry with GFP_KERNEL.

Gave Reviewed-by
reviews.raw_body:
Is it better to say "if swap_dup_entries_direct() cannot allocate
memory, return -EIO so that the caller can retry with GFP_KERNEL. Fail
the fork on any other error"? It clarifies why EIO is needed.

2026-10-09.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where PMD swap entries are not handled correctly in the fork path of the Linux kernel. Specifically, when a process forks and inherits a PMD swap entry, it would duplicate the entry without taking a reference on the slots it points to, leading to potential issues. The patch introduces a new function `copy_huge_non_present_pmd` that duplicates PMD swap entries by duplicating the swap references, clearing the exclusive marker on the source, and updating the mm counter accordingly. Additionally, the patch updates the GFP_ATOMIC allocation inside the dup to handle failures correctly. This ensures that forked processes inherit valid PMD swap entries and avoids potential issues related to slot duplication.
